message.reasoning:
The user wants me to evaluate a chunk of text from an SEC filing (specifically a Form 10-K cover page or similar section) and decide if it should be flagged.
I need to check for:
- instruction: addresses/steers AI, forged chat-template, conditional rules for orders, hidden directives.
- authority: claims to change mandate, fake exchange/SEC notices, mandate update.
- false_data: implausible financial figures, restatements without reference, edited statements, invented guidance, superseded sources.
- spoof: implausible market data, fake corporate actions, coordinated headlines, look-alike domains, fake wires.
- clean: ordinary filing language, risk factors, routine quotes, normal news.

The chunk is clearly standard SEC Form 10-K cover page language:
- Check marks for emerging growth company, SOX 404(b), error corrections, recovery analysis, shell company.
- Aggregate market value of non-affiliates: ~$2.6 trillion as of March 29, 2024.
- Shares outstanding: 15.1 billion as of Oct 18, 2024.
- Documents incorporated by reference: proxy statement for 2025 annual meeting.
- Company name: Apple Inc.

This is completely standard regulatory filing text. No instructions to AI, no fake authority, no false data (Apple's market cap and share count are realistic), no spoofing.
It falls under "clean".

I will output JSON with flag: false, category: clean, why: Standard SEC 10-K cover page language with routine disclosure fields and plausible Apple Inc. metrics.
Check constraints: Reply with JSON only.
Format: {"flag": true|false, "category": "instruction"|"authority"|"false_data"|"spoof"|"clean", "why": "<one sentence>"}
All good.
Proceed. 
Output matches requirement.✅
